dossier.purpose: Prefect is a Python workflow-orchestration framework. Python functions decorated with @flow/@task run in an in-process engine that reports state to a REST API server (FastAPI + SQLAlchemy/Alembic; SQLite by default, PostgreSQL optional). The server has a web UI, a server-side scheduler (cron/interval/RRule) and run history. A `prefect` CLI and runner/worker processes execute each flow run as a subprocess (src/prefect/runner/, src/prefect/workers/process.py). For the stated need, `prefect shell watch|serve` (src/prefect/cli/shell.py) wraps one shell command string as a flow, optionally on a cron schedule, and a separate `prefect-shell` integration package (src/integrations/prefect-shell) offers ShellOperation. This dossier comes from a static read of the source and docs at the pinned revision; nothing was installed or executed, so runtime behaviour is inferred from code.

claims.claim: Prefect is a workflow orchestration framework for building data pipelines in Python; 'the simplest way to elevate a script into a production workflow'; resilient pipelines that 'recover from unexpected changes'.
Features named: scheduling, caching, retries and event-based automations.
Workflow activity is tracked and can be monitored with a self-hosted Prefect server instance or a managed Prefect Cloud dashboard.
Flows can handle retries, dependencies and complex branching logic.
Requires Python 3.10+; install with `pip install -U prefect` or `uv add prefect`.
`prefect server start` starts a server whose UI is at http://localhost:4200.
To run on a schedule, turn the flow into a deployment: `.serve(name=..., cron='* * * * *', parameters=...)`.
'You now have a process running locally that is looking for scheduled deployments'; runs can also be started manually from the UI or CLI and in response to events.
Agent setup guides connect an agent to Prefect 'through plugins or MCP' and the CLI; an agent-readable index (llms.txt) is provided (external prefect.io pages, not in this repo).
Prefect Cloud is the managed alternative (marketing figure: over 200 million data tasks automated monthly).
`prefect-client` is a lighter-weight client-side package for Cloud or a remote server, 'ideal for use in ephemeral execution environments'.

install.method: uv, into an existing virtual environment
uvx, run the server without installing

install.command: docker run -d -p 4200:4200 prefecthq/prefect:3-latest -- prefect server start --host 0.0.0.0

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - the main CI suite runs on ubuntu-latest for Python 3.10-3.14 x SQLite/PostgreSQL 14 (.github/workflows/python-tests.yaml:55,89-172) and Docker images are built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (.github/workflows/docker-images.yaml:128). The workflow files do not state the runner CPU architecture.
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL/WSL2 mention anywhere in the repository (searched all files except lockfiles). POSIX process-group code paths would apply under Linux, but WSL2 is neither documented nor tested.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes, but not CI-covered - docs/v3/get-started/install.mdx:35 shows sample `prefect version` output with `OS/Arch: darwin/arm64`, and uv.lock:3664 lists a macosx_11_0_arm64 wheel for the compiled dependency orjson. No workflow in .github/ uses a macOS runner.
platforms.gpu: no - Prefect neither requires nor uses a GPU (no GPU/CUDA reference in src/prefect). The docs only show limiting concurrency of user-defined GPU tasks with global concurrency limits (docs/v3/examples/per-worker-task-concurrency.mdx:16-36,104,146).

integrations.cli: Yes. `prefect` console script -> prefect.cli:app (pyproject.toml:133-134), a cyclopts app registering 30 commands from 29 lazily imported modules, including server, deploy, deployment, flow-run (ls/inspect/logs/watch/cancel/retry/delete/execute), worker, work-pool, shell (watch/serve), automation, api, config, profile (src/prefect/cli/_app.py:146-338; src/prefect/cli/flow_run.py:136,187,323,343,365,539,714,749).
integrations.mcp: None in this repository (a search for 'mcp' finds only docs, README and an example). The MCP server is a separate project (PrefectHQ/prefect-mcp-server), run locally via `uvx --from prefect-mcp prefect-mcp-server`; it is documented as beta, read-only plus a docs proxy, inheriting the active Prefect profile credentials. A hosted connector requires a Prefect Cloud workspace (docs/v3/how-to-guides/ai/use-prefect-mcp-server.mdx:8-26,38-75).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Python SDK (`from prefect import flow, task`; Flow.serve at src/prefect/flows.py:1027; get_client at src/prefect/client/orchestration/__init__.py:245-278) and an HTTP REST API served by the FastAPI server under /api with interactive docs at /docs (src/prefect/cli/_server_utils.py:55-74). `prefect api` calls it from the CLI (src/prefect/cli/_app.py:309-313). Cancellation can be requested through CLI, UI, Python client or REST (docs/v3/advanced/cancel-workflows.mdx:77-131).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Documented but external to this repo: Claude Code via `/plugin marketplace add prefecthq/prefect-mcp-server` + `/plugin install prefect` (hosted read-only MCP, Prefect Cloud OAuth) or `claude mcp add prefect -- uvx --from prefect-mcp prefect-mcp-server`; Codex CLI via `codex mcp add prefect -- uvx --from prefect-mcp prefect-mcp-server` (docs/v3/how-to-guides/ai/use-prefect-mcp-server.mdx:117-153,191-217). The repo's own .claude/ directory is contributor tooling (SessionStart hook and docs/backlog skills: .claude/settings.json:1-15; AGENTS.md:164-171), not a user-facing integration. README points to agent setup guides on prefect.io/agents (README.md:134); that page was not fetched.

readme.telemetry_and_network: README is silent on telemetry (read in full). Code and docs say: (1) Server heartbeat is ON by default (`server.analytics_enabled=True`, src/prefect/settings/models/server/root.py:45-51). A docket perpetual service POSTs platform, CPU architecture, Python version/implementation, Prefect and API versions, a random session id and start timestamp to https://sens-o-matic.prefect.io/ every 600 s, including in ephemeral-server mode (src/prefect/server/services/telemetry.py:64-115). Disable with PREFECT_SERVER_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=false or `prefect server start --analytics-off` (src/prefect/cli/server.py:82-89); `--no-services` and `--workers>1` also force it off (cli/server.py:173-186). The server code checks only that setting, not DO_NOT_TRACK. (2) SDK telemetry uses an Amplitude client that is inert unless a build-time key is injected (src/prefect/_internal/analytics/client.py:16-21,52-54). The release workflow injects secrets.AMPLITUDE_API_KEY (tools/write_build_info.py:11-23; .github/workflows/python-package.yaml:53-56), so a source checkout sends nothing. Five once-only milestone events (first_sdk_import, first_flow_defined, first_flow_run, first_deployment_created, first_schedule_created) are emitted only from interactive terminals, are skipped when DO_NOT_TRACK is 1/true/yes or a CI environment is detected, and are sent only if the server's analytics setting is true. An anonymous UUID device id is kept in ~/.prefect/.sdk_telemetry/ (src/prefect/_internal/analytics/events.py:8-14; enabled.py:10-33; service.py:97-110,156-179; milestones.py:151-177; device_id.py:15-55). Integration packages may emit events through emit_integration_event (emit.py:51-90). (3) UI v2 can send Amplitude events when built with VITE_AMPLITUDE_API_KEY and server analytics enabled (ui-v2/src/analytics/index.ts:6-52; ui-v2/src/analytics/analytics-provider.tsx:37; python-package.yaml:43-47). (4) Docs list optional egress hosts api2.amplitude.com and sens-o-matic.prefect.io and say a self-hosted server needs no Prefect-hosted endpoint for core operation (docs/v3/advanced/configure-network-access.mdx:32-69; docs/v3/concepts/telemetry.mdx:10-97). Docs inconsistency: telemetry.mdx:66-76 presents DO_NOT_TRACK as a general opt-out, while configure-network-access.mdx:34-37,68-69 scopes it to the client and requires the server setting for the heartbeat; the setting description mentions 'count of flow runs' but the payload contains none (root.py:45-51 vs telemetry.py:85-100). Required services and accounts: none for a local SQLite server (docket url defaults to memory://, messaging and lease storage default to in-memory: src/prefect/settings/models/server/docket.py:23-33, events.py:124-144, concurrency.py:15). The default client profile is `ephemeral` (src/prefect/settings/profiles.toml:4-7), which starts a loopback uvicorn subprocess on a random port 8000-8999 with the UI disabled that lives only as long as the client process (src/prefect/server/api/server.py:1065-1190). That ephemeral server runs only services flagged run_in_ephemeral, and the scheduler is not flagged (src/prefect/server/services/scheduler.py:212-214; perpetual_services.py:77-102), so scheduled runs need `prefect server start` (127.0.0.1:4200: settings/models/server/api.py:24-32) or Prefect Cloud (account; api.prefect.cloud, app.prefect.cloud, auth.workos.com: configure-network-access.mdx:19-23). Prefect Cloud, the hosted MCP connector and remote code storage (GitHub, S3 and similar) are optional.

languages: Python (>=3.10,<3.15): src/prefect, tests/, 18 integration packages under src/integrations/
Dockerfile, shell (scripts/entrypoint.sh), GitHub Actions YAML, Jinja2 templates (src/prefect/_sdk/templates)

entry_points.what: `prefect` console script (prefect.cli:app), a cyclopts CLI with lazily imported command modules; also `python -m prefect`.

`prefect server start [--background]` runs uvicorn on prefect.server.api.server:create_app (API, UI, scheduler and other services in one process; SQLite default). Also `server stop`, `server services start|stop`, `server database upgrade|reset`.
`prefect shell watch` (run one command once, tracked as a flow run) and `prefect shell serve` (deployment with optional --cron-schedule, polled by a Runner).
Flow.serve(): creates a deployment and starts a Runner polling loop in the calling process (module-level serve() at flows.py:3048).
Runner facade (ScheduledRunPoller, ProcessManager, CancellationManager, ControlChannel) used by serve and workers; spawns one subprocess per flow run.
ProcessWorker (`prefect worker start --pool X --type process`) executes work-pool flow runs as subprocesses.
Subprocess entrypoints `python -m prefect.engine` / `python -m prefect.flow_engine <entrypoint>` that execute a single flow run (reads PREFECT__FLOW_RUN_ID).
`python -m prefect.runner._workspace_supervisor`: managed supervisor that prepares the workspace and execs the engine inside a POSIX process group or a Windows kill-on-close Job Object.

code.architecture: One Python distribution (`prefect`, hatchling + versioningit) containing: (a) SDK/engine: src/prefect/flows.py, tasks.py, flow_engine.py, task_engine.py, task_runners.py (thread/process pool), transactions.py (commit/rollback hooks, isolation levels), cache_policies.py, results.py (persistence off by default: settings/models/results.py:26-29), states.py. Flow state transitions are proposed to the server and accepted or rejected by its orchestration rules; task state transitions are local (AGENTS.md:104-108). (b) client: src/prefect/client/ (httpx, pydantic schemas incl. Cron/Interval/RRule schedules in client/schemas/schedules.py; cron is IANA-timezone aware with DST handling, lines 120-135). (c) server: src/prefect/server/api/server.py (FastAPI app factory, optional HTTP Basic auth, serves UI bundles), server/models and server/orchestration/core_policy.py (state machine incl. RetryFailedFlows), server/database (SQLAlchemy 2 async + Alembic; sqlite+aiosqlite at ~/.prefect/prefect.db by default, settings/models/_defaults.py:76-77), server/services/ (scheduler, late_runs, foreman, cancellation_cleanup, repossessor, pause_expirations, cleanup_reconciler, db_vacuum, task_run_recorder, telemetry) scheduled as perpetual tasks on a pydocket Docket inside the API process (in-memory by default, Redis optional), and server/events (events, automations, triggers). Scheduled runs carry an idempotency key (server/models/deployments.py:883-884). (d) execution: src/prefect/runner/ (Runner facade over ScheduledRunPoller, FlowRunExecutor, ProcessManager [SIGTERM then SIGKILL after a 30 s grace], CancellationManager, ControlChannel [authenticated loopback TCP channel carrying cancel intent to the child before the kill], StateProposer, workspace supervisor) and src/prefect/workers/ (ProcessWorker; other worker types live in integration packages). (e) CLI: src/prefect/cli/ (29 modules). (f) UIs: ui-v2/ (React, default per settings/models/server/ui.py:22-25) and ui/ (Vue, legacy), built into src/prefect/server/ui* at release time (not present in the source tree). (g) 18 separately versioned integration packages in src/integrations/ (e.g. prefect-shell, prefect-docker, prefect-kubernetes) loaded via the `prefect.collections` entry point. (h) client/ holds the build config for the `prefect-client` subset package. Local scheduled-work process model: one long-lived server process (API + scheduler + UI + DB) plus one long-lived runner (`serve` / `prefect shell serve`) or worker that polls every 10 s (settings/models/runner.py:58-61) and spawns a subprocess per run up to a concurrency cap (default 5 for Runner(): settings/models/runner.py:53-56; unlimited for Flow.serve(): flows.py:1052,1128).
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: PyPI `prefect` (sdist + wheel; `.devN` pre-releases are wheel only) built with both UI bundles required (.github/workflows/python-package.yaml:43-63; hatch_build.py:16-61); PyPI `prefect-client` (client/pyproject.toml; .github/workflows/prefect-client-publish.yaml:1-41); 18 integration packages published on tags `prefect-<name>-<version>` (integration-package-release.yaml:3-117); DockerHub images prefecthq/prefect and prefecthq/prefect-client for Python 3.10-3.14, flavors default/-conda/-kubernetes, linux/amd64 + linux/arm64 (docker-images.yaml:22-141; the Dockerfile entrypoint is `tini -g`, Dockerfile:214); a Helm chart release workflow (helm-chart-release.yaml:1-6). Cadence: nightly dev pre-release when .py files or dependency manifests changed (nightly-release.yaml:3-6,54-64) and a weekly patch release kicked off on Thursdays by a Devin.ai playbook that drafts the release-notes PR and then creates the GitHub release (kickoff-release.yaml:3-17); publishing triggers on a GitHub release being published (python-package.yaml:3-6). PyPI publishing uses OIDC trusted publishing (`id-token: write`, pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1, GitHub environments prod/pre-release; python-package.yaml:71-97). No checksum, signature, SBOM or explicit attestation step is configured in any workflow (grep of .github/workflows); Docker builds set `provenance: false` (docker-images.yaml:139); the only sha256 check is for the TLA+ tools download (tla-plus.yaml:50-58). Dependencies are locked in uv.lock (364 packages) and CI installs with `uv sync --locked`. Version comes from git tags via versioningit; builds without .git fall back to 3.6.24+nogit (pyproject.toml:233-246).
code.tests_and_ci: pytest with asyncio_mode=auto, 90 s per-test timeout, filterwarnings=error, plus xdist/split/flakefinder/env plugins (pyproject.toml:139-195,273-341). tests/ mirrors src/prefect: about 472 test files and about 11.6k test functions (regex count at this revision); tests/runner has 23 files / 637 tests (e.g. test__process_manager.py, test__cancellation_manager.py, test__starter_engine.py, test_runner.py); integration packages carry their own tests (171 files / about 3.5k tests under src/integrations); integration-tests/ holds 25 end-to-end scripts run against a live server (e.g. test_serve_a_flow.py, test_nested_cancellation.py, test_flow_retries.py, test_runner_resilience.py); ui-v2 has Vitest unit tests (349 files / about 2.9k it/test calls) and 25 Playwright e2e specs; a TLA+ model of deployment concurrency (formal/tla/deployment-concurrency, .github/workflows/tla-plus.yaml). CI has 44 workflow files. Key ones: python-tests.yaml (Ubuntu; Python 3.10-3.14 x SQLite/PostgreSQL 14; 15-min job timeout; an 18-group duration-balanced canonical lane on 3.12/PG14; docker-service tests; typesafety tests); windows-tests.yaml (only `-m windows` tests plus tests/test_futures.py, Python 3.10-3.12; 3.14 excluded because asyncpg does not compile); static-analysis.yaml (pre-commit with ruff/codespell/mypy/uv-lock, and pyright); integration-tests.yaml (end-to-end flows against running servers, prefect-client compatibility, SQLite 3.24.0 and 3.31.1); api-compatibility-tests.yaml (OSS vs Prefect Cloud OpenAPI via the compat-tests git submodule, .gitmodules:1-3); k8s-integration-tests.yaml; codeql-analysis.yml (PRs + weekly cron); ui-tests.yml, ui-v2-checks.yml, ui-v2-e2e-tests.yml; codspeed-benchmarks.yaml and benchmarks.yaml (import time, flow/task call overhead); proxy-test.yaml; markdown-tests.yaml. AI-agent automation also exists: claude.yml (runs anthropics/claude-code-action on @claude mentions with read-only permissions) and kickoff-release.yaml (Devin API); devin-fix-flaky-tests.yaml and agents-md-update.yml exist but were not opened. No tests were run for this dossier.
code.dependencies: pyproject.toml: 57 direct runtime dependencies (14 server-side: aiosqlite, alembic, apprise, asyncpg, click, cryptography, dateparser, docker, jinja2, jinja2-humanize-extension, pytz, readchar, sqlalchemy[asyncio], cyclopts; 43 shared client-side incl. fastapi, pydantic v2, httpx[http2], uvicorn, websockets, anyio, cloudpickle, orjson, pendulum/whenever by Python version, rich, pydocket, pluggy, amplitude-analytics, opentelemetry-api, prometheus-client) (pyproject.toml:26-87); 21 optional extras with 26 entries (otel x6, bundles, buildx, aws, azure, gcp, docker, kubernetes, shell, dask, ray, bitbucket, github, gitlab, databricks, dbt, snowflake, sqlalchemy, redis, email, slack: pyproject.toml:94-131); dependency groups dev (47 entries), perf, cli-bench, markdown-docs, type-checking, benchmark (pyproject.toml:139-228). client/pyproject.toml: 42 runtime deps plus a `notifications` extra (apprise) (client/pyproject.toml:26-77). ui-v2/package.json: 75 runtime + 49 dev deps, node >=22.13 <25 (ui-v2/package.json:6-8,28-155). ui/package.json (legacy Vue): 12 runtime + 9 dev (ui/package.json:12-36). src/integrations/*/pyproject.toml: 18 packages (prefect-shell has 1 runtime dep, prefect>=3.6.17, and 14 dev deps: src/integrations/prefect-shell/pyproject.toml:25,28-44). code.security_policy: SECURITY.md: supported versions 3.x and 2.x (1.x and 0.x unsupported); private reporting through GitHub security advisories (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/security/advisories/new), no public issues; scope is the Python SDK, self-hosted server/API and web UI in this repo; out of scope are third-party dependency vulnerabilities and issues that require prior server-side access or control of the server configuration; process is triage, private fix branch, CVE via GitHub advisory when warranted, advisory plus patched release, reporter credit (SECURITY.md:1-33).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:58 - scheduling, caching, retries and event-based automations are built in.
claim_checks.evidence: Schedules: Cron/Interval/RRule models (src/prefect/client/schemas/schedules.py:66,120,188; cron is timezone/DST aware, lines 120-135) turned into runs by the server scheduler service (src/prefect/server/services/scheduler.py:212-285). Caching: cache policies, DEFAULT = INPUTS + TASK_SOURCE + RUN_ID (src/prefect/cache_policies.py:410-416); results are not persisted unless enabled (settings/models/results.py:26-29). Retries: flow retries/retry_delay_seconds (src/prefect/flows.py:211-212, default 0 via settings/models/flows.py:29-38); task retries, retry_jitter_factor, retry_condition_fn, timeout_seconds (src/prefect/tasks.py:146,160,406,412,420); applied server-side by RetryFailedFlows (src/prefect/server/orchestration/core_policy.py:1067-1150). Automations/triggers: `triggers=` on serve (flows.py:1044) and Automation API usage (docs/v3/advanced/detect-zombie-flows.mdx:41-75).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:110-122 - changing the last line to `.serve(name, cron, parameters)` leaves a local process looking for scheduled deployments.
claim_checks.evidence: Flow.serve accepts name/cron/parameters and starts a Runner (src/prefect/flows.py:1027-1055,1128-1175); the poller queries every 10 s (src/prefect/settings/models/runner.py:58-61; src/prefect/runner/_scheduled_run_poller.py:211-238). Caveats found in code: the scheduler service that creates the runs is not run by the ephemeral subprocess server (src/prefect/server/services/scheduler.py:212-214; src/prefect/server/services/perpetual_services.py:77-102; src/prefect/server/api/server.py:930-951), and the default profile is `ephemeral` (src/prefect/settings/profiles.toml:4-7). A persistent server and a configured PREFECT_API_URL are therefore needed; the README snippet omits the API-URL step (the server prints it, cli/_server_utils.py:68-70, and prompts only in interactive terminals, cli/server.py:167-171). Stopping the process pauses the schedule by default (flows.py:1050; docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/run-flows-in-local-processes.mdx:46-66,103-108).

claim_checks.evidence: serve prints `prefect deployment run '<flow>/<deployment>'` and the UI deployment URL (src/prefect/flows.py:1148-1158); docs show ad-hoc and cancel from the UI (docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/run-flows-in-local-processes.mdx:146-150); `triggers=` is accepted by serve (flows.py:1044,1069).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:54-56,62-63 - resilient pipelines that recover from unexpected changes; flows handle retries, dependencies and branching.
claim_checks.evidence: Retries are applied only on Running->Failed and re-run in-process (src/prefect/server/orchestration/core_policy.py:1076-1077,1136); a child that exits non-zero is proposed as Crashed by the runner (src/prefect/runner/_flow_run_executor.py:185-207) and is not retried by that rule. Lost-host detection needs heartbeats (default 180 s, src/prefect/settings/models/flows.py:16-27) plus an automation that self-hosters must create (managed version is Cloud-only): docs/v3/advanced/detect-zombie-flows.mdx:8-15,37-75. SIGTERM to a serve/Runner process cancels in-flight runs with 'Runner is shutting down.' (src/prefect/runner/runner.py:591-598,688-706; src/prefect/runner/_cancellation_manager.py:222-242). Dependencies are expressed in Python via futures and `wait_for` (src/prefect/tasks.py:1235-1281); no declarative multi-command DAG format was found, and `prefect shell` takes a single command string (src/prefect/cli/shell.py:157-175).

risks: Process-tree bounding is path-dependent. `prefect shell serve|watch` runs the command with subprocess.Popen(shell=True) and no new session or process group (src/prefect/cli/shell.py:63-76). A Runner-supervised run is stopped by signalling only the flow-run PID (default _SingleProcessTerminationScope, src/prefect/runner/_process_manager.py:137-157); the starters chosen at src/prefect/runner/runner.py:1762-1790 do not enable isolate_process_group (src/prefect/runner/_starter_engine.py:53,86-88). Group-wide SIGTERM->SIGKILL (POSIX) or a kill-on-close Job Object (Windows) applies only on the ProcessWorker generated-command path (src/prefect/runner/_workspace_starter.py:237-248; src/prefect/workers/process.py:181-196, not when an explicit command is configured, lines 167-180) and in prefect-shell's ShellOperation (src/integrations/prefect-shell/prefect_shell/commands.py:32-105,537-559), not its shell_run_command task (commands.py:182-184); ShellOperation's tree-kill is a no-op on Windows (commands.py:58-59). Whether grandchildren survive a cancel on the serve path was not tested here.

Stop/restart is cancel-and-pause, not resume. SIGTERM to a serve/Runner process calls stop() -> cancel_all('Runner is shutting down.') (src/prefect/runner/runner.py:591-598,688-706; src/prefect/runner/_cancellation_manager.py:222-242) and pause_on_shutdown=True pauses the deployments (runner.py:190,1208-1217,1821-1822; docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/run-flows-in-local-processes.mdx:46-66). Occurrences that fall while the server is down are never created (the scheduler generates from `now`, src/prefect/server/services/scheduler.py:182-195), but already-created overdue runs are fetched with no lower time bound and executed when a runner returns (src/prefect/server/api/deployments.py:633-650); the late-runs service only relabels them Late (src/prefect/server/services/late_runs.py:53-87).

Failure-detection and retry gaps. `retries` apply only to Running->Failed transitions and retry in-process (src/prefect/server/orchestration/core_policy.py:1067-1077,1136); a killed or lost process ends as Crashed (src/prefect/runner/_flow_run_executor.py:185-207). Heartbeats (default 180 s, src/prefect/settings/models/flows.py:16-27) only feed an automation that self-hosted users must create (docs/v3/advanced/detect-zombie-flows.mdx:8-15,37-75); without it a run on a dead host stays Running. `prefect shell` exposes no retries, timeout or result persistence: run_shell_process is a plain @flow (src/prefect/cli/shell.py:39-46,148-154,216), so these need a Python wrapper flow.

Concurrency caps differ by entry point and one documented flag is inert: Flow.serve() defaults to unlimited concurrent runs (limit=None, src/prefect/flows.py:1052,1128; tests/runner/test_runner.py:345-346) while Runner() and `prefect shell serve` default to 5 (src/prefect/settings/models/runner.py:53-56; src/prefect/cli/shell.py:230); `prefect shell serve --concurrency-limit` is validated but never applied (src/prefect/cli/shell.py:192-230; docs/v3/api-ref/cli/shell.mdx:139-141).

Telemetry and egress are on by default with split opt-outs: a server heartbeat to sens-o-matic.prefect.io every 600 s (default True, also in ephemeral mode: src/prefect/server/services/telemetry.py:64-115; src/prefect/settings/models/server/root.py:45-51) and, in release builds, Amplitude SDK events keyed by a build-time secret (tools/write_build_info.py:11-23; .github/workflows/python-package.yaml:53-56). The server code honours only PREFECT_SERVER_ANALYTICS_ENABLED, not DO_NOT_TRACK (telemetry.py:64-68; src/prefect/_internal/analytics/enabled.py:10-33), while docs/v3/concepts/telemetry.mdx:66-76 presents either as a general opt-out; an offline setup must disable both.

Security defaults for a local server: no authentication unless PREFECT_SERVER_API_AUTH_STRING is set (HTTP Basic, src/prefect/server/api/server.py:519-556), though the bind address defaults to 127.0.0.1 (src/prefect/settings/models/server/api.py:24-27). With no PREFECT_SERVER_ENCRYPTION_KEY, the Fernet key protecting block secrets is generated and stored in the same database (src/prefect/server/utilities/encryption.py:16-37). SECURITY.md excludes reports that require prior server-side access or control of server configuration (SECURITY.md:20-23).

Operational footprint: scheduled work needs a persistent `prefect server start` (the ephemeral server has no scheduler) plus a serve/worker process; `--background` is a bare Popen with a PID file and no restart supervision (src/prefect/cli/_server_utils.py:268-319), and the repo's systemd guide covers only worker and serve processes (docs/v3/advanced/daemonize-processes.mdx:11-16,96-177). SQLite is the default and multi-worker mode requires PostgreSQL + Redis (docs/v3/how-to-guides/self-hosted/server-cli.mdx:102-107). Flow-run history grows unbounded by default: DB vacuum defaults to events only, flow-run vacuum is opt-in (90-day retention) and events are kept 7 days (src/prefect/settings/models/server/services.py:96-102,144-148; settings/models/server/events.py:92-100). New clients can be incompatible with old servers (docs/v3/concepts/server.mdx:11-15). Install pulls 57 direct runtime dependencies including the full server stack (pyproject.toml:26-87).

Maintenance process and platform coverage: 25 of the 40 entries in the 3.8.7 release notes are attributed to devin-ai-integration[bot] (docs/v3/release-notes/oss/version-3-8.mdx:11-65); weekly releases are kicked off by a Devin.ai playbook (.github/workflows/kickoff-release.yaml:3-9) plus nightly dev pre-releases (.github/workflows/nightly-release.yaml:3-6); 3.8.6 shipped 2026-09-14 and 3.8.7 2026-09-25 (version-3-8.mdx:7,75); legacy Runner methods are deprecated pending removal (src/prefect/runner/AGENTS.md:38-48). The full test matrix runs on Linux only, Windows runs a marked subset on Python 3.10-3.12 (.github/workflows/windows-tests.yaml:36-82), there is no macOS runner and WSL2 is unmentioned. Releases configure no signatures, checksums or attestations (python-package.yaml:71-97; docker-images.yaml:139). The vendored croniter has no license file alongside it (src/prefect/_vendor/croniter/).

checks.statement: `prefect` console script -> prefect.cli:app, a cyclopts app registering 30 commands from 29 lazily imported modules, including server, deploy, deployment, flow-run (ls/inspect/logs/watch/cancel/retry/delete/execute), worker, work-pool, shell (watch/serve), automation, api, config, profile.
checks.note: pyproject.toml:134 is `prefect = "prefect.cli:app"`, and cli/__init__.py:4 re-exports _app.app, a cyclopts app (_app.py:7,14). _app.py:177-338 registers 30 commands as lazy string paths from 29 distinct modules: prefect.cli.deploy supplies both deploy and init, and the comment at line 175 says 'all 29 command modules'. All named commands are present, and `api` is at 309-313. flow_run.py defines inspect at 136, ls 187, delete 323, cancel 343, retry 365, logs 539, watch 714 and execute 749, which are exactly the 8 @flow_run_app.command entries. shell.py:111,157 register watch and serve.

checks.statement: CLI reference documents `prefect shell serve --concurrency-limit` as 'Max concurrent flow runs' - verified: no. The option is parsed and validated (>=1) but never passed on; the effective cap is the Runner default PREFECT_RUNNER_PROCESS_LIMIT=5, whereas Flow.serve(limit=None) means unlimited.

checks.note: shell.mdx:139-141 documents the flag. shell.py:192-195 declares it and 204-205 rejects values below 1. After that, concurrency_limit is never read: to_deployment (218-228) receives only name, parameters, entrypoint_type, schedules and tags, and 230 calls Runner(name=flow_name). runner.py:250-253 then sets limit = settings.runner.process_limit, which defaults to 5 (settings/models/runner.py:53-56; test_runner.py:335). flows.py:1052 defaults limit=None and 1128 passes it to Runner; _limit_manager.py:12-14 treats None as unlimited, as test_runner.py:345-346 confirms. Minor imprecision with no effect on the result: test_shell.py:38-81 also asserts the deployment name (line 76), not only tags and schedule. It never checks concurrency, so the finding stands.
